items.question: What should be recognized as the nectar that destroys wrinkles and gray hair?
premises: A prior radiance reaching brahma-randhra is described
That radiance is to be known as nectar
This nectar destroys wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: The ascending radiance is identified as rejuvenating nectar.
uncertainties: balī is taken as wrinkles following legacy hint
items.plain_english: One should know that as nectar, which destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What bodily condition results from knowing and attaining this nectar?
premises: The nectar has rejuvenating power
One can become freed from wrinkles and gray hair
One can become devoid of all diseases
items.inference: Attaining this nectar yields freedom from aging signs and all diseases.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from wrinkles and gray hair, and devoid of all diseases.

items.question: Where should the tongue be applied to bring about the destruction of disease?
premises: A yogic application of the tongue is prescribed
The location specified is the root of the palate
The purpose is the destruction of disease
items.inference: Applying the tongue at the root of the palate serves to destroy disease.
items.plain_english: One should indeed apply the tongue at the root of the palate for the destruction of disease.

items.question: How should the tongue be positioned regularly within one's own mouth during this practice?
premises: The tongue is the object of practice
It should be contracted regularly
It should remain united within one's own mouth
items.inference: The practice requires regularly contracting the tongue and keeping it united within the mouth.
items.plain_english: One should always contract the tongue, keeping it united within one's own mouth.

items.question: What mental placement leads the practitioner to attain the transcendent state beyond mind?
premises: The mind is to be placed in the heart
This placement is maintained over time
The practitioner reaches the state of unmanatā
items.inference: Fixing the mind in the heart leads to the attainment of the transcendent no-mind state.
items.plain_english: Placing the mind in the heart, one continues until reaching the transcendent state beyond mind.

items.question: What well-guarded secret concerning time has now been revealed to the goddess?
premises: The teaching concerns the deception of time
This teaching was well guarded
It has now been made manifest
items.inference: The secret method for overcoming time has been revealed.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the well-guarded deception of time has now been made manifest.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the section concerning emergence from the moon island?
premises: The context is emergence from the moon island
A chapter is being identified
It is designated as the sixth
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the sixth chapter in the moon-island section.
uncertainties: candra-dvīpa-vinirgate may be a colophon phrase with uncertain exact reference
items.plain_english: Thus ends the sixth chapter in the section on emergence from the moon island.

items.question: What teaching about the three principles does the goddess request after taking refuge in the lord?
premises: The goddess addresses the lord as her sole refuge
She has gone to him for refuge
She asks him to explain the three principles
items.inference: Having taken refuge in the lord alone, the goddess requests instruction on the three principles.
items.plain_english: Tell me of the three principles, O Lord; I have gone to you alone as my refuge.

items.question: How should what is located in the goddess's wheel be contemplated in relation to the new moon?
premises: Something within the goddess's wheel is to be contemplated
A comparison is made to the moon on the first lunar day
The contemplation follows this lunar analogy
items.inference: One should contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel as like the moon on the first lunar day.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate what is in the goddess's wheel, just as the moon appears on the first lunar day.

items.question: Where is the subtle flame said to be absorbed within the contemplative locus addressed to the goddess?
premises: The location is specified as there in that context
A flame is described as absorbed
The absorption occurs in the bone wheel
items.inference: The flame is absorbed there in the bone wheel.
uncertainties: asthi-cakre may refer to a specific subtle center; exact identification uncertain
items.plain_english: And there indeed, O beautiful-faced one, the flame is absorbed in the bone wheel.

items.question: What qualities characterize the contemplated form that destroys wrinkles and gray hair?
premises: A form is described for contemplation
It is fluid and black in appearance
It destroys wrinkles and gray hair
items.inference: The contemplated fluid black form has the power to destroy wrinkles and gray hair.
items.plain_english: It is a fluid, black form, and it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

items.question: What kind of yogic application should be practiced in the region of the support base?
premises: A specific bodily location is indicated
Yoga is to be applied there
The yoga is characterized as cool
items.inference: One should apply a cooling yoga in the region of the support base.
uncertainties: ādhāra-skandha-saṃsthāne may refer to a specific subtle locus
items.plain_english: One should apply a cooling yoga in the region of the support base.

items.question: How should the practitioner regard the sun and the moon in this contemplative practice?
premises: The sun is to be visualized in a certain way
The moon is to be visualized in a contrasting way
The attitudes are like enemy and friend respectively
items.inference: The practitioner should regard the sun as an enemy and the moon as a friend.
items.plain_english: One should see the sun as an enemy and the moon indeed as a friend.

items.question: What kind of physical location is suitable for undertaking this yogic practice?
premises: A dwelling place is specified
It should be solitary
It should be free from gnats and mosquitoes
items.inference: The practice should be done in a solitary earthen house free from gnats and mosquitoes.
uncertainties: bhū-gṛhe could mean an underground room or earthen house
items.plain_english: In a solitary earthen house, in a place free from gnats and mosquitoes.

items.question: What further qualities make a place auspicious for this yogic practice?
premises: The place should be secluded and deserted
It should have a divine quality
It should be adorned with an abundance of flowers
items.inference: An auspicious place for practice is secluded, deserted, divine, and adorned with flowers.
items.plain_english: In a secluded, deserted, divine place adorned with an abundance of flowers.

items.question: What level of attainment is realized after six months of this practice?
premises: A time period of six months is specified
Perfection becomes known after this period
The attainment is equal to the state of a yoginī
items.inference: After six months, one attains perfection equal to the state of a yoginī.
items.plain_english: After six months, perfection is known, equal to the state of a yoginī.

items.question: From what knot are the three principles said to be situated, as addressed to the goddess?
premises: Three items are being identified
They are situated from the brahma knot
The statement is addressed to the beautiful-faced goddess
items.inference: The three are indeed situated from the brahma knot.
uncertainties: syntactic relation of ā etāṃ trīṇi is somewhat compressed
items.plain_english: O beautiful-faced one, these three are indeed situated from the brahma knot.

items.question: What substance should be used to permeate the body beginning with the pores?
premises: A fluid substance is to be used
It should color or permeate the whole body
The scope begins with the pores of the skin
items.inference: One should permeate the entire body, beginning with the pores, with this fluid.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one should color the whole body with the fluid, beginning with the pores.

items.question: Within what time frame is the promised result said to occur without any doubt?
premises: A result is asserted to occur
There is no doubt about it
The time frame is within six months
items.inference: The result certainly occurs within six months.
items.plain_english: It indeed happens without doubt, within six months.

items.question: What visual and sonic qualities adorn the contemplated fluid form in this practice?
premises: The form is fluid and black in color
It is adorned with sixteen vowels
These qualities characterize the object of contemplation
items.inference: The contemplated form is fluid, black, and adorned with the sixteen vowels.
uncertainties: varṇañca contains fused sandhi (varṇam + ca) marked by form
items.plain_english: It is fluid, black in color, and adorned with the sixteen vowels.

items.question: What rejuvenating transformation occurs through six months of repeated practice?
premises: The practice is performed repeatedly for six months
Even an old person undertakes it
The practitioner becomes youthful
items.inference: Six months of repeated practice makes even an old person youthful.
uncertainties: taruṇā āyate may be read as becoming youthful; exact form slightly irregular
items.plain_english: Through six months of repeated practice, even an old person becomes youthful.

items.question: What dark-colored form is contemplated after resorting to the place of the yoginī?
premises: One resorts to the place of the yoginī
A form is contemplated there
That form is dark and black-colored
items.inference: After resorting to the yoginī's place, one contemplates a dark, black-colored form.
items.plain_english: Having resorted to the place of the yoginī, one contemplates the dark, black-colored form.

items.question: By what power should the region of the hair, shoulders, and skull be colored in this practice?
premises: The area of hair, shoulders, and skull is specified
It is to be colored
The coloring is done by its radiance
items.inference: One should color the region of the hair, shoulders, and skull by that radiance.
items.plain_english: One should color what is situated in the region of the hair, shoulders, and skull by its radiance.

items.question: What ultimate freedom from aging, death, and illness results from this yogic attainment?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from old age and death
The practitioner becomes devoid of disease and illness
These are presented as resulting conditions
items.inference: The attainment yields freedom from old age, death, disease, and illness.
items.plain_english: One becomes freed from old age and death, and devoid of disease and illness.
